"Eat something green once a week."

"Send the coward to the edge of the world," he said. "Somewhere he can't get anyone else killed."
"Tam is a genius."

"The red sky sleeps."

*SHE WENT TO PLAY IN THE WOLD.*
*SPEAK TO US IN THE ORDER OF A LIFE, AND THE WOLD WILL LET YOU PASS.*
*WE ARE BORN. WE ARE BOUND. WE ARE BURIED.*
A Crest? At her age? Oh, you'll want Old Bethan for that. The cottage up the hill, past the beehives. She knows Crests better than any priest.
A barricade of stolen crates, barrels and one very surprised-looking hay cart. Painted on it: AURENNE ROAD — TOLL — ASK FOR TAM.
A bronze gull spouting water. Someone has knitted it a tiny hat.
A cairn of sea-smoothed stones, stacked with care. Someone built this to last.
A cairn of sea-smoothed stones. A gull feather has been tucked between two of them, carefully.
A cat. A real cat?
A cauldron of something that smells of mint, honey and righteous indignation.
A dense hawthorn hedge. Someone has woven it tight here, on purpose. You can smell rosemary and mint behind it.
A fortnight ago? Sable washed up on Lanternfall barely a _week_ ago.
A hermit named Hesketh, who used to keep the Gull Light, fed us stew and showed us a goat path around the soldiers. He says the light tells you what you are — not what you'll do about it.
A knight who's... still loading.
A little girl named Merry is hiding somewhere in the Whisperwold. She wants to be found.
A lone tree at the edge of the overlook, its violet leaves turned toward the far-off sea.
A man's voice. Warm, and tired, like someone talking in his sleep.

A notebook of names and Crests, in a hundred different inks. The oldest pages are dated sixty years ago. Near the middle, a single line: "C. — the Keeper's boy. Mender, Arcanist, Cantor, Warden. Wants more. Too much more."
A rockfall chokes the top of an old goat path down the cliff. Far below, the cove glitters.
A sack of salted herring. The sack has teeth marks in it. The teeth marks are ginger.

A scarecrow in a battered hat. Its button eyes seem to follow you. That's just a thing people say about scarecrows.
...Isn't it?
A seam of violet crystal runs through the quarry wall like a vein. It is cold enough to hurt, and it is breathing. Someone has been chipping it out by the cartload.
A shelf of sailors' knots, tied and labeled in a careful hand. Bowline. Sheet bend. Clove hitch. The bowline has been tied and untied so many times the rope is frayed white.
A shelf of ships in bottles. One of them is a Dawnguard frigate, built upside down. Mags says it's "accurate".
A slender tree, pale as bone. Its voice is very young.
A small stone, green with moss, half-hidden in flowers that should not be blooming in autumn.
A standing stone, warm to the touch. Voices move inside it like fish under ice.
A tent full of stolen flour sacks, three hats, and a very confused mule.
A tree of violet glass and old bark. It hums, softly, the way a mother hums with her mouth closed.
A voice in the trees at the overlook said "west, always west." It's a common enough thing to say. It's a common enough thing to say.
A wall of black thorns, thick as a man's wrist. Woven, almost. As if someone made it to keep something in — or keep you out.
A wall of roots, twisted together like clasped hands. Behind it, violet light pulses slowly, like breathing.
ADMIRAL! You fat orange traitor! Come here— no, he's gone straight back to her. Of course he has.
Absolutely not.
Admiral Whiskers
Admiral's asleep in the herring crate. He'll be there till spring.
Again! Count again! Big Shiny Man counts too fast. Shawl Lady, you count.
All those years telling me there was nothing out here worth leaving for...
All three scarecrows are down. Tell Farmer Dunstan his fields are safe.
All three? Even Old Strawman? ...Granddad would've hated that. He'd also have hated a walking scarecrow, so. Swings and roundabouts.
Alright! Alright. Yield. I yield. Mercy. Uncle. All the good words.
Also a log. I name the logs. You'd name the logs too, after twenty years up here.
An anvil, polished to a mirror. It has never once been used. "It's for atmosphere," says Tolliver.
An inn. Inns have back doors. Every inn I've ever been thrown out of had a back door.

An innkeeper named Mags hid us from Thorne's Own. Bram told us about his trial — Garrick Thorne called him a coward and sent him to Lanternfall. The soldiers said Sable is to be brought to Aurenne "unharmed".
An oil lamp on the sill, burning low and steady. The glass is spotless. Someone cleans it every single day.
An old tree with a split trunk, hollow and quiet. Fireflies drift in and out of it as if they are visiting.
An old well behind the inn. A bucket, a rope, and a great many wishes at the bottom, some of them probably about cider.
And Pugilist at sixty-one, because a man in Aurenne told me I was too old to learn anything.
And a gift. Cantor — the singer's Crest. Songs that steady the heart. I learned it at forty to annoy that bishop. It'll suit at least one of you.

And here's the bit the Choir hates: a Support you've learned is yours forever. Learn to counter as a Pugilist and you'll still counter as a Mender. Your *Support Points* decide how many knacks you can carry.
And if anyone can talk sense into Red Tam, it's her. He's terrified of her. So am I.
And the Whisperwold's talking louder this year. Louder than I've ever heard it. Make of that what you like. I make nothing of it. I'm in commerce.
And the archer on the ridge says the rest. Back, Wren.
And then she is only a tree: very old, very tired, and quiet at last.
And they came back down again without a single bandit in chains. You tell me what that means. I know what it means. I want to hear you say it.
And when tin-cans come asking after a frightened girl and won't say what she did — she didn't do anything. That's what that means.
And you. Come here, child. Give me that hand.

Answer the voice?
Answer what?
Are you a knight? You look like a knight.
Are you— the Reeve said you're the Crestless Sage?
Ask Bethan for another sparring match?
Asking's free. Answers cost a log-name.
At the heart of the wold stands a tree so old it has forgotten it is a tree.
Auntie Prue
Aurenne. Two days east. Then the Cathedral. Then answers.

BY ORDER OF THE LORD-COMMANDER: any person sheltering a girl of about sixteen years, black hair, pale complexion, is to report to the Dawnguard. REWARD.

Below it: LOST — GINGER CAT. ANSWERS TO "ADMIRAL". (DOES NOT ANSWER.) — Bettany, Fish Market.
Back again? Sit by the fire a while. Agatha's free.
Back already? Pedrick sells Crest Stones. Try a few on. Wear them like hats.
Bed, bath and a bowl of chowder. Thirty gold. Fugitives pay in advance.
Beds are straw, pillows are feathers, soup is mostly turnip. Forty gold. Breakfast is whatever the cat didn't eat.
Beehives, humming. One bee lands on your hand, considers you thoroughly, and leaves unimpressed.
Been waiting nine days. The wind's stubborn this year. Like it's waiting on something too.
Bees are out again. Singing. They knew before I did — they always know.
Before the rocks. Before Lanternfall. I was in the water, and the water was full of voices like these. All talking. None of them listening.
Behind the barrel, wedged into a gap no cat should fit, is a great deal of ginger cat. One ear points at heaven.
Behind the barrel: a dent in the dust the exact shape of a smug cat.
Bethan sent you after Tam? Of course she did. She sends everyone after something.
Bethan taught you, then? ...Forty years I've been a Vanguard who weaves. Maybe I'll go up the hill tomorrow.
Bethan's herb path? Pulled the hedge back myself. Far east end of the fields, then up the hill.
Bethan's mad. ...I think about it, though.

Bethan, the Crestless Sage, has FIVE Crests. She says "one Crest, one life" is a lie, and taught us to braid our Crests. She once taught a Keeper's son who lost someone young. She wonders if she made a monster.
Bethan... why did the Choir really throw you out?
Bettany's ginger tom fled when the soldiers searched the fish market. Somewhere dark, near fish...
Better. Not good. Better.
Big Hollis
Big Shiny— I— One. Two. Three...
Black hair! Lieutenant! LIEUTENANT, IT'S HER—
Black-sailed cutter tied up at my pier four days ago. No harbor fee. No manifest. "Dawnguard business."
Books the Choir tried to burn. Some of them are singed at the edges. One is titled _On the Braiding of Callings, and Why the Cathedral Is Wrong About Everything_.
Bought new stuffing for 'em off some lads on the road. Two silver a sack. Purple, it was. Glittery. Swore it'd keep the crows off for good.
Bram hasn't said a word in an hour. Is that a record? We should write it down.
Bram. You know them. Thorne's Own.

Brother? ...Brother, I can't find the door. It's so dark.

But the Hierophant says something wonderful is coming. A dawn like no other. I believe him. I've always believed him.
By the black pond, a crooked tree with a split like a grin. Something in it laughs — a wheezing, honking laugh, like a seal choking on a herring.
Bye, Big Shiny Man. Bye, Grumpy— I mean, bye, Ilse. Bye, Wren.
Bye, Sable. Don't let anybody keep you.
